instructions: Heat the oven to 200°F and put a foil lined baking sheet in it. Line a plate with paper towels.
Pull the skin off the chicken and shred 3 cups of the meat with your fingers. Save the rest of the chicken for another meal.
In a bowl, mix the chicken with the 1 cup cheese, 1/2 cup of the salsa, the can of green chiles, the 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 tsp of the salt and the 1/4 tsp pepper.
Stack the 12 tortillas on a plate, cover them with a damp paper towel and microwave for 30 seconds. Warm tortillas roll without cracking.
Spoon about 1/3 cup of the filling in a line along the bottom of each tortilla. Roll it up tightly and push a toothpick through the seam to hold it closed.
Shred half the head of lettuce and dice the 2 tomatoes.

Pour the 3 cups oil into a large, deep skillet. It should be about 3/4 inch deep. Heat it over medium to 375°F. No thermometer? Dip the end of a flauta in. The oil is ready when it bubbles hard around it straight away.

Using tongs, lower 4 flautas into the oil seam side down and hold each one for a few seconds until it firms up. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes, turning them, until they're golden brown all over. Stand back a little. They'll spatter.
Move them to the paper towels and sprinkle a little of the remaining 1/4 tsp salt over them while they're hot. Keep them warm on the baking sheet in the oven while you fry the rest the same way.
Pull out the toothpicks. Taste a flauta. If it's flat, sprinkle on a pinch more salt.
Serve the flautas on the lettuce and tomatoes, with the sour cream and more salsa on the side.
method_notes: All three roll shredded chicken tightly in tortillas and fry them in about an inch of oil, 2 to 3 minutes, until golden. Lil' Luna mixes cooked chicken with Mexican blend cheese, salsa, canned green chiles, garlic salt and pepper, rolls it in 6-inch flour tortillas held with toothpicks, fries at 375°F and salts them hot, which this version follows. Pati Jinich warms corn tortillas on a comal so they don't crack, fills them with plain chicken and tops them with lettuce, queso fresco, crema and salsa, and The Modern Proper poaches its own chicken and mixes it with chipotle in adobo, sour cream and lime.
